The dividend payout ratio of 96% of earnings and a yield above 12% is unsustainable given declining earnings and high leverage.
Net interest income has fallen 11.4% annually over the past five years, and the net interest margin has hovered near breakeven for two years, indicating erosion of profitability.
A declining hedge ratio increases Annaly’s sensitivity to rate changes, worsening the outlook for rising rates.
Non‑QM impairments rose 16 basis points in May 2026 and the 2024 vintage shows higher delinquencies, raising credit risk.

implications.why: Higher mortgage application and refinance volumes increase demand for agency MBS, boosting asset yields.
Steepening yield curve allows Annaly to refinance at lower short‑term rates while earning higher long‑term MBS yields, widening net interest spread.
Strong demand and limited supply of high‑quality agency MBS let Annaly maintain or slightly raise coupon spreads over risk‑free rates.
If short‑term rates rise, interest expense on debt increases, compressing net interest margin.
Short‑term liquidity needs are modest and largely offset by high liquidity in the agency portfolio.
